subject: Post-demo: deployment mode and migration follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)
messages:
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Marin <sofia@novacorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment mode and migration follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side while this is still fresh: we heard that NovaCorp is evaluating three options for serving production traffic — Redwood Hosted API, Reserved Dedicated pools, and Private VPC (customer-managed). You and Alex mentioned a migration from a self-hosted cluster ("LegacyCluster") with steady inference spikes during end-of-quarter reporting.

Notes / clarifying questions:
- Traffic profile: current p95 latency targets are ~250ms for short-text generation and you have occasional bursts up to ~600 RPS (peak 5–10m windows). Please confirm burst duration average.
- Data residency & connectivity: Private VPC required for EU PII datasets; otherwise you can use hosted in us-west for non-PII traffic. Do you need a hybrid route (some endpoints private, some hosted)?
- Model compatibility: you referenced a stack built on Falcon-40B self-hosted with custom tokenizer. Are you planning to keep that same model family or consider a Redwood-curated variant?
- Auth & keys: will SSO or customer KMS/HSM integration (for Private) be required on day one?
- Procurement timing: you mentioned procurement window in Q4 — any dates we should align to for provisioning Dedicated capacity?

Attachments: I attached a short inventory template (migration-inventory-template.xlsx) — can you/your infra lead fill the red sections: current RPS, model names, tokenizer specifics, and network egress constraints? Also attaching a draft Dedicated SLA for procurement review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alex or infra lead fills inventory template (target by Wed 9/17).
2) Technical deep-dive with PrIyom (solutions engineering) to validate model compatibility and sizing (we have 90-min slots next week).
3) We'll produce a provisional cost/latency comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your peak profile and two migration scenarios (lift-and-shift Falcon-40B vs switch to Redwood-curated 40B quantized).

I copied Jordan to track contracts/procurement asks. If Hybrid is likely, highlight which endpoints must be private.

Thanks — Kim

Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment mode and migration follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)

Thanks Kim — good recap. A few quick answers inline: 

> Traffic profile:
We typically see sustained 60–90 RPS across user-facing features and predictable spikes to ~650 RPS for reporting jobs that run for 6–12 minutes. Those jobs are batchable but we'd like <1s latency for interactive calls.

> Data residency & connectivity:
We do need EU private routing for PII (customer support transcripts) and low-latency us-west for product features. Hybrid looks likely.

> Model compatibility:
We plan to keep the Falcon-40B stack initially — we use a patched tokenizer and a small post-processing hook. We can share the tokenizer repo.

> Auth & keys:
KMS for Private is mandatory; SSO (SAML) for user access is preferred but not blocking.

> Procurement timing:
We are in procurement now; target internal approval by 2025-10-20 for a Nov provisioning.

I'll take the inventory template and loop in our infra lead (Alex). Expect an update by next Wed.

— Sofia

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-demo: deployment mode and migration follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick answers. A few technical clarifications from the SE side so we can size and propose migration options accurately: 

1) Tokenizer & model tarballs: can you share the tokenizer repo and a sample model checkpoint (or a small distilled checkpoint) via a private S3 link or share a model signature (vocab size, tokeniser class)? We can't guarantee 1:1 behavior with quantized variants unless we validate tokenization and sampling.

2) Reporting jobs: are they currently using long-context windows (>4k tokens) or sliding-window approaches? If >4k routinely, Dedicated or Private with larger memory GPUs is recommended.

3) KV cache persistence: do you require persistent KV across requests (session affinity) for user chat state? That affects routing and capacity planning.

4) Egress & throughput: any hard egress caps from your datacenter? If Hybrid, we'll need to estimate cross-region traffic for private endpoints.

If you can provide the inventory and a sample model/ tokenizer by 9/17, I'll prepare two sizing sketches: (A) lift-and-shift Falcon-40B on Dedicated (estimated GPU and token cost) and (B) compacted quantized variant in Hosted with cache/batching knobs to hit latency targets.

I'll set up 90-min booking links; Kim, can you propose 3 slots next week?

Thanks — Priyom
